bibliography.title: Improving the ionic conductivity in nanostructured membranes based on poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA), chitosan (CS), phosphoric acid (H 3 PO 4 ), and niobium oxide (Nb 2 O 5 )
bibliography.authors: D. A. Quintana 1   &  E. Baca 1,2   &  E. Mosquera 1,2   &  R. A. Vargas 1,2   &  J. E. Diosa 1,2

mechanism_relevant_findings: The enhancement of ionic conductivity is attributed to the introduction of Nb2O5 particles which create defects and free volume in the polymer matrix.
Blending of PVA with chitosan improves ionic conductivity due to better compatibility and intermolecular interactions.
The ionic transport mechanism is influenced by structural changes in the polymer matrix upon doping with Nb2O5 and H3PO4.

numerical_findings.conditions: at 130 °C for the sample with 6% Nb2O5

limitations: The study does not explore the long-term stability of the membranes under operational conditions.

relevance_judgement.reason: The paper provides significant experimental data supporting the understanding of proton conduction mechanisms.
